 Let’s cut to the chase. If there is any justice, sanity or logic in football then Harry Kane will win the Ballon d’Or when the ceremony takes place in London on Monday.
 Arsenal would have deservedly won this Champions League match away to Bayern Munich if Kane was not on the pitch. Instead, they almost lost it but for another bit of brilliance from Declan Rice, Kane’s vice-captain for England, and probably his successor to wear the armband.
 A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥
📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Y25zI80A0z
— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 21, 2026 
 “I’m lucky I can play with him and not so lucky I have to play against him,” Rice said, and that summed it up succinctly.
 And that Ballon d’Or? There is bias, but Rice – who is also on the 30-strong list of nominees – added of Kane: “He is the clear winner. His numbers speak for themselves, the year he has had has been remarkable. When you play with him you realise how good he is and when you play against him you see how much of a pain it is.”
 Arsenal stood toe-to-toe with Bayern in an open match. Both sides went for it, partly because they knew under the Champions League format, that defeat was not a disaster. There has been some chat about whether Arsenal can be, well, a bit dull. Not here. It would be no surprise to see these two face off again deep into this competition.
 The only setback for Arsenal was a worrying injury to Bukayo Saka early on, limping off and tapping his thigh, indicating an issue with his muscle. Mikel Arteta’s reaction betrayed his understandable concern.
 Bukayo Saka hobbled off after the Arsenal winger picked up an early knock
 Credit : Getty Images/David Price
 Kane won a penalty and then expertly took it to give Bayern the lead. Other strikers could have scored the penalty but few would have created the wonderful assist that drew Bayern level.
 It has been a fact for quite some years that Kane is not only the best goalscorer for England but the best passer. Indeed, if Kane could provide for Kane he would have scored even more goals.
 “ Unsere nummer neun ,” shouted the stadium announcer after Kane’s goal and that needed no translation. Kane is a god in Bavaria, where they know a few things about having great centre-forwards. But the 33-year-old is surpassing them all.
 Kane’s goal meant he had scored in 10 straight Champions League games, one short of the record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. It was also the former Tottenham Hotspur forward’s 16th goal in 23 games against Arsenal. No one has ever scored more against them.
 Kane earned a penalty, before coolly slotting it home to put Bayern ahead
 Credit : Reuters/Kai Pfaffenbach
 Kane is the complete player, carrying out his defensive duties – winning headers to clear Bayern’s lines from Arsenal free-kicks – to linking the play to being the focus of his team’s attacks. He is a centre-half, central midfielder and centre-forward. Who pops up on the wing to deliver pinpoint crosses.
 Maybe Kane will be pipped at the Palladium – the theatre where the ceremony takes place – by Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal or Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé, or even an absurd sympathy vote for Lionel Messi. But Kane deserves it. His time is now.
 Some passages of play in the first half deserve analysis. Just to highlight how good Kane was. After an Arsenal corner, wastefully volleyed over by Riccardo Calafiori, Bayern countered and suddenly it was three on two. Serge Gnabry, the former Arsenal winger, had to do better than shoot weakly when picked out on the overlap. David Raya saved. That was a let-off.
 But who sprung that counter? It was not Manuel Neuer, the Bayern goalkeeper, taking the goal-kick, but Kane, with his sharp thinking. And then Kane launched a superb pass from deep which Ismael Saibari should have dealt with better. It should have been another opportunity. Potentially a goal.
 Is there anything Harry Kane can't do? 🧐
His goal kick very nearly led to a Bayern Munich goal 😲 https://t.co/fqbsN7KOjw
— Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) October 21, 2026 
 And then Bayern did score. The ball was played inside to Kane, in centre field and afforded too much space. He delivered a perfectly weighted through ball for Alphonse Davies to run on to. The pace was perfect, allowing the Canadian not to break stride and stroke it past Raya. Kane did not fire the ball in, he did not make Davies work to reach it and he did not give Jurrien Timber any chance of cutting it out. It was perfect. Few players could do that. “Harry Kane puts the ball in a space from 30 metres that doesn’t exist,” Arteta said. True.
 Harry Kane with an OUTRAGEOUS assist, and Alphonso Davies equalises 🥵
📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/6cGXrUloHW
— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 21, 2026 
 It was Saka’s replacement who gave Arsenal the lead, Eberechi Eze profiting from Martin Odegaard’s perceptive, lofted pass and taking advantage of Bayern’s ragged defending and some suspect goalkeeping from 40-year-old Neuer to score from an angle. Initially it was ruled out for offside, but that was overturned after a VAR check to provide Eze with a bit of redemption after being hooked against Nottingham Forest at the weekend.
 VAR has given it, and Eze strikes Arsenal into the lead at the Allianz 🔥
📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/i1LjrZVnbI
— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 21, 2026 
 Neuer had his own slice of redemption as he saved well from Bruno Guimarães’ close-range header, pushing it against a post with Raya also excelling to beat out another header, this time from Dayot Upamecano.
 When Timber was punished for handball, as he blocked Kane’s shot, the penalty was given. Up stepped Kane and we knew the rest. At that point it felt like Bayern would win, but Arsenal continued to play courageously and pushed on, as they had done throughout, risking conceding further goals.
 Harry Kane, what a penalty 🥶
He scores in his TENTH consecutive Champions League game to give Bayern the lead 😳
📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/4k4jPCQEWF
— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 21, 2026 
 They were rewarded as Rice started the move, playing the ball in quickly to Noni Madueke with substitute Viktor Gyokeres laying it back into the midfielder’s path. He strode on and Neuer was again beaten from an angle. It was certainly warranted, even if it did not detract from Kane’s night. But will he have a greater one on Monday?
 Latest updates 
 Jason Burt. 
 Sam Dean
 at Allianz Arena. 
 Daniel Zeqiri
 live updates
 10:52PM
 Kompany’s assessment
 Link copied to clipboard 
 It had similarities [with last year’s league phase game]. I think we managed to create more chances but I think that Arsenal – and it’s something that has been mentioned by them before the game – they’ve worked a lot on retaining the ball and making it difficult to get the ball back. We did feel that.
 It was a game in chunks. They had moments, we had moments. In our moments, I think we exploited the spaces in behind a little bit better maybe but we played against a top team and the result is a result between two big teams.
 10:43PM
 Arsenal currently in the top eight
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Last year they reaped the benefits of a top-two finish: home ties all the way to the final and a guarantee of avoiding the other club in the top two.
 They have a chance to pick off Real Madrid at the Emirates, and will anticipate Aston Villa (who still have to play Barcelona and PSG) and Real Betis dropping points.
 Given PSG have already dispatched Manchester City and Barcelona, it is hard to envisage them dropping a point, though they do have the odd off night.
 Arsenal’s chances of grabbing second could come down to winning their remaining games and Liverpool slipping up. But with five games to go, these permutations are probably premature.
 10:39PM
 Arteta on the performance
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Wow, what a game. That is one of the highest levels that we have played. The level of opposition, what the game required, and our level as well. Two teams who wanted to press each other and wanted to attack and wanted to play. It was a fascinating game.
 I think we started the game incredibly well, we were so dominant, we did everything to deserve the first goal. We didn’t score the goal and lost Bukayo and had to adapt to it.
 We gave a terrible chance away after our corner which could have cost us, then we scored the goal. In the second half, the game was even,  they started probably a little bit better before they scored and they you have to react and we certainly did.
 The spirit of the team, the quality we have showed on the second goal as well.
 Mikel Arteta was pleased with his team’s efforts
 Credit : PA/Adam Davy
 10:28PM
 Arteta on Saka’s injury
 Link copied to clipboard 
 They are a bit concerned. A player having to come off with a sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see.
 Bukayo Saka appears set for weeks on the sidelines
 Credit : Reuters/Kai Pfaffenbach
 10:20PM
 Rice endorses Kane for the Ballon d’Or
 Link copied to clipboard 
 For me he’s the clear winner, his numbers speak for themselves. He’s obviously up against some other world class players. When you play with him you see how good it is, and when you play against him you see how much of a pain he is! As a striker to play that pass for the goal... he’s ridiculous. Lucky I can play with him, not so lucky when I have to play against him.
 10:13PM
 Kane’s reaction
 Link copied to clipboard 
 I thought it was a good performance. Probably the draw was a fair result overall. We probably just didn’t get quite enough right tonight to get the win.
 Nice to get the assist to get back into the game and then I thought we had some good moments but not enough over the 90 minutes.
 Harry Kane troubled Arsenal again
 Credit : Reuters/Kai Pfaffenbach
 10:12PM
 Rice on his goal and the tactical battle
 Link copied to clipboard 
 When you play against teams like Bayern who are man to man all over the pitch you have to apply certain principles, and I just kept running and managed to get away from my man. When they are following you all over, I just kept running and I was in on the goal.
 He’s been making such a good impact from the bench [Gyokeres]. He’s made some great runs tonight and set me up for the goal. When you play against man to man, who follow you everywhere over the whole pitch, it’s such a tough game. You have to apply certain principles and concepts, and you’re constantly thinking about where the space is. For the goal, Noni one-touch set, Viktor’s one-touch set, those little movements put you through on goal.
 10:08PM
 Finding the right balance
 Link copied to clipboard 
 In periods of the game, it felt like Arsenal were trying to play in the manner of Bayern or PSG by leaving themselves so light at the back with acres of green grass to cover. 
 Would they play like that in a quarter-final? Probably not, and they were emboldened by Bayern missing some key players. But it helped them create danger and have some strong spells, even if there were some scary moments going the other way.
 Somewhere between that display and Arsenal’s rearguard in the Champions League final is probably the sweet spot.
 9:53PM
 FT: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 2
 Link copied to clipboard 
 A high-quality game between two of the most plausible winners of this season’s Champions League finishes level.
 It was a helter-skelter contest at times. For all the talk of Arteta being a conservative coach, Arsenal committed numbers forward in their press and when they attacked, and that left them vulnerable to Bayern’s fast transitions and Kane’s passes from deep.
 Perhaps it is a missed opportunity to beat Bayern in the Allianz, given the German side started without Olise, Kimmich, Musiala and Diaz, but a point from the hardest fixture of the league phase is more than acceptable.
 The fly in the ointment is the injury suffered by Saka in the first half, but Eze and Madueke performed well in his absence.
 Declan Rice finished a well-worked Arsenal move
 Credit : Shutterstock/Anna Szilagyi
 9:52PM
 92 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 2
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Just one minute to play and Bayern have the ball in Arsenal’s half, but Calafiori gets his foot in. Madueke does well to keep it and Lewis-Skelly finds Eze.
 9:50PM
 91 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 2
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Timber with dig from outside the box after a poor defensive header from Bayern, and Neuer tips it over. Rice to take the corner, and Arsenal’s set-pieces have caused problems throughout. This might just be Arsenal’s chance to win it.
 Swung to the back post, but Tah did enough.
 9:49PM
 90 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 2
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Bayern had an injury worry of their own now: Luis Diaz, not judged fit to start, has pulled up and will have to come off. Bayern were in a promising position in the Arsenal half. 
 Three minutes of added time to play.
 9:48PM
 89 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 2
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Harry Kane looking for another of those arced passes forward, but Eze read it and retrieved. Arsenal finishing the stronger when it comes to possession and territory. Perhaps that Premier League intensity bearing fruit as the game progresses.
 9:46PM
 87 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 2
 Link copied to clipboard 
 A couple of fouls given away by both teams, it has been a bitty few minutes. But Arsenal do well to find Lewis-Skelly free in the middle of the pitch, and he finds Rice who drives the away team forward.
 9:44PM
 84 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 2
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Neither team appears inclined to settle for the draw, but Arsenal have the wind in their sails. Mikel Merino is on for Martin Odegaard, who has probably been Arsenal’s best player on the night.
 9:42PM
 GOOOALLL! Rice buries an equaliser after slick move
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Arsenal back level again, and it is an emphatic finish across Neuer from Rice, after a deft touch from Gyokeres around the corner at the edge of the box. Bright football around the box from Arsenal. Still 10 minutes or so to play.
 Arsenal have been scoring gorgeous team goals all season. They have done so in all three of their Champions League games this season. They were labelled as “boring” after the Forest victory but that game was the exception, rather than the rule, on the evidence of this campaign. 
 A brilliantly worked team-goal finished off by Declan Rice, and Arsenal are level 💥

 9:39PM
 79 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Arsenal deep in Bayern territory after Rice’s cross towards Eze glanced off the head of a defender. Bayern are keeping a good defensive shape though, Arsenal finding it difficult to penetrate. Arteta is preparing another pair of changes.
 9:37PM
 76 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Luis Diaz with a snap shot that brings a sharp save from David Raya. On the balance of chances and threat created, Bayern have earned their lead. But still plenty of football to play. Arsenal have not scored from a set-piece this season, but they have looked dangerous tonight. They need another couple.
 Neuer has just smashed into Stanisic, sweeping up a long ball Timber was chasing.
 With Tzolis out and Saka now likely to be joining him on the sidelines, at what point does Arteta turn to Dowman in the league and Champions League? Obviously there are so many physical and defensive demands that are very difficult for a 16-year-old to meet... but the talent is there.
 9:33PM
 74 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Arsenal enjoying plenty of territory and possession now, but you’d say Bayern look more likely to score on the counter-attack. Arsenal content to keep the ball and set themselves for a late assault.
 9:31PM
 71 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Lewis-Skelly with a no-touch turn in midfield but then he takes too long and Bischof wins the ball cleanly. Davies nutmegs Rice on the counter, but Madueke tracked back diligently to snuff out the danger. At the other end, Karl fouls Eze who has enjoyed a strong game, aside from his goal.
 9:28PM
 68 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Karl and Diaz are on for Bayern, replacing Gnarby and Saibari. If anything that shifts Bayern up a gear. Arteta has also made a double change: Lewis-Skelly on for Guimaraes, and Gyokeres on for Havertz.
 The more open and transitional this game has become, the less comfortable Arsenal have looked. I’m not surprised Arteta has taken off Guimarães, as they have been struggling in that midfield battle for much of this second half. It feels like Bayern have taken this game to a place that Arsenal did not quite want to go: lots of space, lots of running, lots of interchanging positions. 
 9:27PM
 65 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Laimer with a foul on Eze near the left-corner of the penalty area, so Arsenal have a free-kick in a promising position for a cross. Havertz, Konsa, Gabriel and Timber the targets.
 Brilliant deliver from Odeegard, somehow Arsenal fail to apply the finishing touch from a few yards out.
 Bayern then escape and stream forward on the break, and Laimer snaps a shot wide.
 9:23PM
 63 minutes: Bayern Munich 2 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Arsenal looking a little shaken at the back after conceding the goal, but Raya is fouled from the corner which helps them clear their lines. Luis Diaz is about to come on for the home team.
 9:20PM
 GOOOAALLL! Kane converts from the penalty spot
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Bayern Munich lead for the first time on the night. Kane with a short stutter, before sending Raya the wrong way and wrapping the shot into the back of the net with power.
 Harry Kane, what a penalty 🥶
He scores in his TENTH consecutive Champions League game to give Bayern the lead 😳
📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/4k4jPCQEWF
— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 21, 2026 
 9:19PM
 BAYERN PENALTY!
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Laimer’s pull back deflected into the path of Harry Kane, and Timber had his arm raised as he slid in to make the block. The referee wasted no time to give the penalty, and there are few complaints. Kane with the chance to score a ninth penalty against Arsenal. Raya up against him.
 There was little controversy around Bayern’s penalty
 Credit : PA/Adam Davy
 9:17PM
 57 minutes: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Bruno Guimaraes and Odegaard with some silky touches to help Arsenal win a free-kick in midfield. Arteta has some of his subs warming up, though he has already used one with Saka going off early on.
 9:14PM
 54 minutes: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Arsenal close to a second goal again, after neat football involving Guimaraes and Havertz to release Eze on the left, and Neuer stuck out a leg to help Bayern scramble the ball away. It would be a surprise if this finished 1-1.
 That’s a few times in this game that Arsenal have been ripped open after all going forward for a corner. It’s very uncharacteristic for Arteta’s side, who are usually so solid in their defensive shape.
 9:12PM
 52 minutes: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 The game continues to be very open, but some of that is the quality on show from both teams. Will Arteta call off the dogs at some point and tell his players to sit off in a defensive shape, or will they keep swinging punches?
 9:10PM
 50 minutes: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Now Raya makes a world-class save at the other end! Upamecano skipped through the Arsenal press and there was acres of space to exploit again. Gnabry stood up a cross to the back post and Raya made a point-black save from Saibari’s header. It looked like he had to score from six yards.
 9:08PM
 48 minutes: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 What a save from Neuer! Down low to keep out a Guimaraes header from the corner. He was reaching back to the goal-line and he plucked the ball up on to the bar.
 Arsenal were then stretched on the counter, but Saibari was offside.
 9:06PM
 47 minutes: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Kane almost produced another great through ball within 30 seconds of the restart, but Gabriel made an interception. Arsenal need Bruno Guimaraes to be on the ball, on a couple of occasions he has been caught in space when Bayern come forward.
 Arsenal respond though, and Arsenal win a corner through Eze.
 9:05PM
 We’re back under way!
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Bayern kick off in the second half.
 9:03PM
 A half-time change made by Kompany
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Tah replaces Kim at centre-back, so a like for like change.
 8:57PM
 Watching back the Bayern equaliser
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Arteta will be very disappointed by how Bayern were able to find Kane free in the middle from a throw-in. Whether Konsa should have been higher or Madueke further across, it was too simple.
 8:50PM
 HT: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 A high-wire act from both teams, who are pushing numbers forward with and without the ball. Lots of man-to-man duels all over the pitch, and when one is lost there is loads of space to exploit. It has made for an entertaining half, and 1-1 is a fair scoreline. Arsenal controlled the first 25 to 30 minutes, but Bayern have looked dangerous.
 The bigger story for Arsenal is the thigh injury suffered by Saka. It would be very surprising to see him before the November international break, at best. He pulled up abruptly.
 Eberechi Eze and his Arsenal team-mates celebrate the opening goal
 Credit : David Price/Getty Images
 8:47PM
 45 minutes: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Lovely Bayern move, whenever they reach three or four passes against Arsenal’s man-to-man pressure they have runners flying forward. Gnabry takes on a shot from a tight angle, and it deflects behind for a corner. Raya does well to claim.
 8:44PM
 43 minutes: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Alphonso Davies’ pace is causing Arsenal some problems, and now it is Bayern’s turn to have a corner. Arsenal have lost some of their control of the first 30 minutes, but still look dangerous themselves. Timber is fouled from the corner, Arsenal free-kick.
 8:42PM
 41 minutes: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Odegaard with a poor pass in the middle of the park, but Konsa produced a tremendous block to stop Kane’s left-footed shot across Raya.
 Within 10 seconds, Arsenal are at the edge of the Bayern box through Rice and they win a corner after Eze’s shot was blocked.
 The corner is flicked to the back post, where Calafiori was inches away from scoring from six inches out. Close to Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.
 8:40PM
 39 minutes: Bayern Munich 1 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 The game is stretched now and quite entertaining, a very different feel to Arsenal’s Premier League assignments. Konsa realised Arsenal were short of numbers and lunged in against Harry Kane, hacking him down at the expense of a booking. Rice and his team-mates recovered well against the counter in any case.
 8:36PM
 GOOOAALL! Davies equalises for Bayern
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Kane with another superb pass, perfectly curled around Timber into the path of Alphonso Davies who finishes beyond Raya. Kane had too much space in the middle of the pitch, Madueke perhaps guilty of not narrowing in.
 Kane has played some absolutely absurd passes in this first half and that was the best yet. Alphonso Davies is so quick that Arsenal were never going to catch him, and the pass was so good that David Raya could not come to it.
 Harry Kane with an OUTRAGEOUS assist, and Alphonso Davies equalises 🥵
📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/6cGXrUloHW
— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 21, 2026 
 8:35PM
 34 minutes: Bayern Munich 0 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 A word of warning for Arsenal is that Kompany has Lennart Karl and Luis Diaz sat on his bench. At least one of those attackers will be on at half-time unless something changes.
 8:33PM
 32 minutes: Bayern Munich 0 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Arsenal winning most of the aerial battles and duels for second balls at the moment, Bayern not building any pressure or fluency. There has been the odd flash of danger when Kane flips a pass in behind but Arteta’s team are comfortable at the moment.
 Odegaard almost finds Eze with a lovely disguised through ball.
 8:30PM
 29 minutes: Bayern Munich 0 Arsenal 1
 Link copied to clipboard 
 There was a 30-second flurry from kick-off where Bayern had Arsenal’s penalty area under siege, but Arsenal have controlled the game well since and they have another corner. Odegaard has enjoyed the extra space on offer all game. Arsenal’s captain whips the corner to the back post where Guimaraes was free, but he shins a volley wide.
 That makes two goals in three games for Eze. Although he got hooked at half-time in one of them (against Forest on Sunday). It feels like that’s probably how it’s always going to be with a player like him, to be honest. Highs and lows.
 8:28PM
 GOAL STANDS! Bayern 0 Arsenal 1 through Eze
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Arsenal had to wait for the VAR intervention, but they have the lead in the Allianz thanks to a high-quality goal. Odegaard released Eze in behind with a lovely ball forward, and the former Palace man steadied himself before drilling a left-footed shot across Neuer.
 VAR has given it, and Eze strikes Arsenal into the lead at the Allianz 🔥
📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/i1LjrZVnbI
— Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 21, 2026 
 8:26PM
 25 minutes: Bayern Munich 0 Arsenal 0
 Link copied to clipboard 
 Good work from Odgegaard in midfield, one lovely flick to help Arsenal restore some control.
 Then Eze puts the ball in the net with a fine finish across Neuer but the flag goes up for offside. This will be checked by VAR... Stanisic, the Bayern left-back, was lingering behind his team-mates on the opposite side of the pitch.
 8:23PM
 23 minutes: Bayern Munich 0 Arsenal 0
 Link copied to clipboard

 Arsenal have plenty of Champions League history with Bayern Munich
 Link copied to clipboard 
 After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.
 Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.
 The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.
 Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.
 A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.
 They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.
 Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.
 Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.
 However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.
 With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.
 For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino. 
 Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.
